chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Ibrahim ibn Mahzar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahzar, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Durostawayh, from 'Ajlan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three [groups] whom God will admit to Paradise without reckoning, and three whom God will admit to Hell without reckoning. As for those whom God will admit to Paradise without reckoning: a just Imam, an honest merchant, and an elder who spent his life in obedience to God, the Mighty and Exalted. And as for the three whom God will admit to Hell without reckoning: an unjust Imam, a lying merchant, and an adulterous elder.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people who enter Paradise without reckoning according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the direct divine reward for three archetypes of virtue: a just Imam, an honest merchant, and a devoted elder, contrasting them with their corrupt counterparts who face immediate Hellfire. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual integrity of leadership, commerce, and aging, suggesting that consistent practice of these roles can bypass the rigorous individual accounting (hisab) on the Day of Judgment. The 'without reckoning' aspect signifies a special grace for those whose lives were defined by these specific, sustained states of piety or vice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-1 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ibrahim ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of his brother Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Fuzalat ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Durostoyeh, on the authority of Ajlan that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

There are three groups of people whom God will let into Paradise without any Reckoning, and three whom God will throw into Hell without any Reckoning. The three whom God will let enter Paradise without any Reckoning are just leaders, honest businessmen and elderly men who have spent their whole life in obedience to the Honorable the Exalted God. And the three whom God will throw into Hell without any Reckoning are the unjust leaders, businessmen who lie, and elderly adulterers.”
